column1: # Tensor-op result latency: ptxas (CUDA 13.1 V13.1.115) emission vs sm_89 GPU measurement.
# Resolves the HMMA/IMMA result-latency divergence between two numbers seen
# downstream: a "13" band entry and a "27-28" completion latency.  Measured on
# an NVIDIA RTX 1000 Ada Generation (sm_89) with ptxas -arch sm_89 + nvdisasm
# -c (control words) + a Driver-API patch-and-relaunch sweep.
# VERDICT.  Neither 13 nor 27 is "the stall ptxas emits".  HMMA/IMMA/BMMA are
# COUPLED tensor ops: ptxas sets NO write-scoreboard on them (dst_wr_sb=7) and
# the dependent consumer carries NO scoreboard wait, so the producer->use order
# is held purely by summed fixed usched stalls.  ptxas spaces the dependent
# consumer 23 issue-cycles after the producing HMMA/IMMA (8+7+8 on the m16n16k16
# lowering) -- the emitted spacing, consistent with the 27-28 result-latency
# model and NOT with 13 (13 is the control/CC issue band, mis-applied to tensor).
# The GPU then shows the spacing is a hardware floor, not a software contract:
# patching the HMMA/IMMA->use issue gap down to 3 still reproduces the baseline
# result bit-for-bit (the tensor pipe interlocks the read), whereas the same
# harness corrupts an under-stalled FFMA chain (4->1) -- proving the probe is
# sensitive and that, unlike scalar FFMA, the tensor read is HW-enforced.
# DMMA is the exception: ptxas tracks it with a real write-scoreboard
# (dst_wr_sb=1, consumer wait on that SB) -- DECOUPLED, matching its 25-26 band.
# coupled_or_scoreboard : how ptxas enforces producer->use ordering
#   coupled    = fixed usched stall, no write-scoreboard (HMMA/IMMA/BMMA on Ada)
#   scoreboard = sets a write-scoreboard, consumer waits on it (DMMA on Ada)
#   group_sb   = warpgroup/group async scoreboard (Hopper/Blackwell, static only)
# source_model   : result-GPR (RAW) latency band the latency model carries
# ptxas_emitted  : producer->dependent-consumer issue-cycle spacing ptxas emits
#                  (m16n16k16 lowering: stall(prod)+stall(prod2)+stall(addr))
# gpu_min_required : smallest still-correct producer->use issue gap on sm_89
#                    silicon from the patch-down sweep (below it the HW interlock
#                    still holds, so the result never breaks => "3+ (HW-locked)")
